nodes.title: T1 · Finite certificate and minimal orbit
nodes.summary: Exact kernel equality has a finite certificate; minimal models differ by normalized hidden similarity.
nodes.intuition: The data pin visible coordinates. Hidden coordinates may change, but physical positivity must still be checked.
nodes.statement:
Finite certificate and minimal orbit. Two models of dimensions n,n' have equal kernels iff R T^k B=R'T'^k B' for 0<=k<n+n'. This follows by Cayley–Hamilton on diag(T,T'). Define linear minimality by full reachability span{T^k Bv} and observability intersection ker(RT^k)={0}. Equivalent minimal realizations have the same dimension and are related by a unique invertible similarity. With the resolved pair fixed, the similarity is S=diag(I_2,U), U1=1, and

\[
Q'=S^{-1}QS,\qquad X'=XU,\ H'=U^{-1}HU,\ Y'=U^{-1}Y.
\]

U need not be nonnegative. Physical offdiagonal positivity and reciprocal support must still be checked. The hidden block partition is Q=((A,X),(Y,H)). Invertibility of T and T1=-B1 prove normalization. See [compatibility proof](compatibility-orbit.md). This lemma is prior realization theory specialized to the prescribed event maps; semialgebraicity or similarity alone does not count F_C(D).
nodes.why_it_matters: Turns the inverse problem into constraints on a finite-dimensional orbit without confusing coordinate equivalence with generator uniqueness.
limitations: Minimality is required for exhaustive similarity, not finite-jet equality or the forward similarity construction.
Signed similarities are allowed. Larger nonminimal models need not lie in the orbit.
Similarity and semialgebraicity alone do not count physical models.
falsification_attempts: Stochastic-only similarity restrictions omit exact physical counterexamples.

novelty.summary: Prior realization theory specialized to fixed resolved event maps; no broad novelty claim.

nodes.verification_scope: Independent conventional proof/scope review is recorded in the linked audit. Saved checks corroborate specified identities and examples; manifest matching is not itself independent verification.
assumption_notes: The finite-jet and similarity algebra does not need the even-state/single-channel entropy convention; that is retained physical context.
Minimality is required for the single normalized similarity orbit, not for the sufficient finite derivative equality certificate.

nodes.title: T2 · Three-state recovery from three Laplace arguments
nodes.summary: Every irreducible three-state source has a locally rational rate inverse with no rate priors.
nodes.intuition: Three bounded transform tests recover the hidden decay, then all physical rates; differentiation need not be continuous in TV.
nodes.statement:
Exact finite-Laplace inverse. For every Q0 in C_3 and any fixed 0<lambda1<lambda2<lambda3, the values of Psi-hat at these three arguments determine Q0 uniquely within C_<=3. On a neighborhood of those values, the inverse restricted to admissible data is rational with nonzero denominators and is locally Lipschitz. Consequently, for Q_n in C_<=3, weak convergence of their row laws to O(Q0) implies eventually N_n=3 and Q_n->Q0 entrywise. Under d_TV convergence the inverse is locally Lipschitz. Neither observed rates, trace, upper rate bounds nor strictly positive triangles are assumed beforehand.

To specify the inverse, write

\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}-r-a&r&a\\s&-s-c&c\\b&d&-b-d\end{pmatrix},\quad h=b+d.
\]

Here r,s>0, a,b>=0 with a=0 iff b=0, c,d>=0 with c=0 iff d=0, and a+c>0. Let P swap mark rows, F(lambda)=P Psi-hat(lambda), H(lambda)=F(lambda)^-1. Schur complementation gives

\[
G_x=\{(H1)_x-1\}/\lambda=1/r+(a/r)/(\lambda+h),\quad
G_y=1/s+(c/s)/(\lambda+h).
\]

Choose a row G=u+v/(lambda+h) with v>0 at Q0. Its three differences give

\[
R_0=\frac{G_1-G_2}{G_2-G_3}\frac{\lambda_3-\lambda_2}{\lambda_2-\lambda_1},\quad
h=\frac{\lambda_3-R_0\lambda_1}{R_0-1}.
\]

For each row i set v_i=(G_i1-G_i2)(lambda1+h)(lambda2+h)/(lambda2-lambda1), u_i=G_i1-v_i/(lambda1+h). Then r=1/u_x,s=1/u_y,a=v_x/u_x,c=v_y/u_y. Fix the branch using the source entrance: if a0>0 use d=-r H_xy(lambda1)(lambda1+h)/a,b=h-d throughout its neighborhood; otherwise c0>0, and use b=-s H_yx(lambda1)(lambda1+h)/c,d=h-b throughout. Both leaves are covered without dividing by a newly opened entrance tending to zero. Two-state candidates have constant G rows and cannot approach the nonzero source differences. Full proof, including nonsingularity and weak-topology justification: [stability audit, Section 3](publication-stability-audit.md#3-new-exact-finite-laplace-inverse-remove-the-prior-rate-cap).
nodes.why_it_matters: Separates stability of rate reconstruction from stability of entropy evaluation.
limitations: Both leaf orientations are covered by fixing the inverse branch using a positive source entrance.
No uniform condition number or minimality of three transform arguments is asserted.
A higher state cap invalidates the result. Observed rates, trace and upper bounds are recovered rather than assumed.
falsification_attempts: Independent direct resolvent checks include both leaves, fast hidden exits and unequal scales.
The earlier sufficient rate cap was removed using bounded Laplace tests, not an invalid differentiation-continuity claim.

novelty.summary: Useful physical-rate inverse; canonical inversion and HMM inverse-learning results are established antecedents.

nodes.title: T2a · Positive triangles have continuous entropy
nodes.summary: A strictly positive three-state triangle has locally Lipschitz entropy in row TV.
nodes.intuition: Nearby recovered rates stay positive, so stationary probabilities and logarithms vary smoothly.
nodes.statement:
At every complete Q0 in C_3, thermodynamic entropy is locally Lipschitz in d_TV and continuous under weak row-law convergence among C_<=3. At a tree, the generator inverse has the same regularity but entropy need not be locally bounded. The previous common-rate-cap proof of E058 is valid but its cap is unnecessary for joint-kernel data. For stationary d_H the saved sufficient common cap remains part of the proved positive result; its removal is open.

Small examples: all six rates one gives a stable equilibrium triangle. The unit tree x-y-h has r=s=c=d=1,a=b=0; its inverse is locally Lipschitz but T4 below defeats every entropy ceiling. C_2 itself has sigma identically zero. A C_2 source under the enlarged cap three is a different boundary; the rare-hidden-state example in [E058](../evidence/RECORDS.md#e058) is unstable. Enlarging the cap above three invalidates T2a by hidden-state splitting. No claim of minimality of the number three Laplace arguments is made.
nodes.why_it_matters: Provides the stable regime in the all-N local-ceiling classification.
limitations: At a tree the same rate inverse is regular but entropy can be unbounded nearby.
Cap-free continuity from a single stationary finite window is open; the saved positive window result assumes a common rate cap.
Local continuity does not imply a globally honest almost-surely finite upper confidence limit.
falsification_attempts: The fixed-trace unit-tree sequence defeats extension to paired-zero boundaries.
Hidden splitting defeats extension to larger admissible state counts.

nodes.title: T3 · Two-point entropy fiber and sharp transition
nodes.summary: The balanced theta family has unbounded, two-point, then singleton entropy fibers across an exact quartic threshold.
nodes.intuition: A global invariant-triangle constraint leaves one connected model at equality. A separate disconnected model survives with different entropy.
nodes.statement:
Balanced-theta theorem. In C_<=5 consider, in order (x,y,h,k,l),

\[
Q(z)=\begin{pmatrix}-11&1&2&0&8\\2&-20&0&7&11\\3&0&-7&4&0\\0&6&5&-11&0\\z&z&0&0&-2z\end{pmatrix},\quad z>0.
\]

Let z_* be the unique positive root of 352z^4-3168z^3-4644z^2-11340z-7623. Every source has linear minimal order five. For 0<z<z_* the entropy fiber is unbounded. For z>z_* the generator fiber is a singleton. At z=z_* the generator fiber has exactly two elements modulo hidden labels, Q(z_*) and Q_*, and its entropy image has exactly two distinct finite points with certified enclosures

\[
\sigma(Q(z_*))\in[.062946400236,.062946400237],\qquad
\sigma(Q_*)\in[.065579685966,.065579685967].
\]

Q_* is defined exactly, without rounded entries, by the rational exit-chart formulas (3)–(6) of [the endpoint specification](theta-balanced-boundary.md#independent-path-coordinate-construction). Equivalently the equality-cone construction in [publication endpoint audit, Section 5](publication-endpoint-audit.md#5-exact-cone-construction-independently-matches-the-path-witness) defines it over Q(z_*,sqrt(6)) and all sqrt(6) coefficients cancel. Its seven reciprocal edges differ from the source's six. Thus the two generators cannot be relabelings. This referenced exact algebraic definition is part of the statement.

Proof obligations and status: minimality forces all cap-five competitors into T1's orbit; Perron normalization exhausts every connected hidden support by a nondegenerate finite triangle; a global envelope quadratic has discriminant a negative positive-factor multiple of the stated quartic; its equality case forces one triangle; separate residue/reciprocity arguments exhaust disconnected hidden supports as the source. Exact feasibility and rigorous logarithm remainders supply existence and entropy separation. A strict-cone construction below the fold overlaps the earlier subcritical theorem, including separately handled repeated poles. [Fresh independent audit](publication-endpoint-audit.md) verifies all of these, including an independent coefficientwise equality between the cone and path constructions.

The unique positive quartic root is approximately 10.5571496686650; the numerical value is illustrative. z=0 is excluded because the source ceases to be irreducible. Hidden pole coincidences at 2z=9+-2sqrt(6), the chart zero z=2 and the earlier first-order threshold are not missing cases: the separate constructive covering handles them. The endpoint is away from these degeneracies. nodes.statement:
Sufficient regularity and the exact mechanism. Fix a reciprocal graph G and a compact set K of irreducible generators with support exactly G. Suppose every admitted sequence with O(Q_n)->D0 has hidden relabelings with dist(Q_n,K)->0 and support(Q_n)=G eventually. Then continuity of pi and sigma on this support stratum gives a finite local upper ceiling: otherwise choose sigma(Q_n)>n at data distance <1/n and extract a limit in K, contradicting continuity. If sigma is constant on K, entropy converges to that value. The positive minimum of the G-rates over K supplies a uniform floor; eventual equality of the competitors' support forbids newly opening edges that vanish in the limit. This is a sufficient condition, not asserted necessary or novel. T2 verifies it locally for a triangle. T4a falsifies the provisional weaker formulation requiring only a compact irreducible limiting set: its limit is the unit tree with positive present rates, while vanishing new chords carry divergent entropy. T5 shows bounded trace alone does not supply this support-controlled inverse property.

An explicit uniform bound is simpler: if all supported rates lie in [m,M], m>0, then sigma<=A log(M/m), where A=sum_i pi_i sum_(j!=i)q_ij is stationary activity. A<=(N-1)M and also A<=tau when trace is fixed. This follows from the directed entropy identity; no stationary probability floor is required. A uniform ratio bound q_ij/q_ji<=R together with A<=Amax suffices instead, with sigma<=Amax log R. A lower individual-rate floor is therefore stronger than necessary when trace or activity is controlled. Ratios alone do not bound entropy: a three-cycle with clockwise rates 2c and reverse rates c has pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3), sigma=c log2 and A=3c, diverging as c increases while R=2. This is a coarse established-type bound, not a novel sharp thermodynamic inequality. Trace tau is not activity A.

views.title: How much dissipation can remain hidden?
views.description: Resolved observation coverage controls exact complete-source entropy fibers and local upper ceilings; the five-state sparse fiber remains a separate result.

reading.title: The answer in one minute
reading.text: At complete networks, all but at most one vertex must be covered: then two positive transform matrices recover Q. Two uncovered vertices permit an exact entropy half-line with fixed trace and observed rates. Sparse sources have no local ceiling when support can open, except for a calibrated zero-budget singleton. Novelty is separated from the proved mathematics.

views.title: From microscopic rates to an entropy set
views.description: Follow the physical chain Q → π → current → σ, alongside the observational chain Q → Ψ → model fiber → entropy identified set.

reading.title: An inverse image, then a scalar image
reading.text: The observations do not directly return entropy. They define a class of compatible generators; evaluating the same microscopic entropy functional on all of them produces an identified set. Its local enlargement is a separate stability question.

views.title: What each theorem actually uses
views.description: Choose a claim to expose its assumptions, supporting lemmas, checks and consequences. Assumption edges state retained scope; they do not assert that every condition is necessary.

reading.title: The source of apparent contradictions
reading.text: Strict positivity gives local entropy continuity at a three-state triangle. Unknown support permits sparse chord openings at a tree. With two fully hidden states, observational ambiguity produces unbounded neighborhoods even near a complete source. Fixed N, a cap on N, a bound on rates and a lower rate floor must never be conflated.

views.title: A claim is stronger than a successful calculation
views.description: Select a claim. Proof, symbolic identity, saved independent verification and numerical discovery are separate evidence roles; raw provenance appears only when you request it.

reading.title: How to read evidence status
reading.text: The project results have conventional proofs with independent checks. The exact endpoint entropy intervals have certified enclosures. High-precision examples and finite search outcomes are corroboration or discovery, not full-support exclusion proofs. No scientific Lean theorem has been checked.

views.title: Failures changed the shape of the theory
views.description: The arrows distinguish a failed proposal, its exact counterexample, and the revised scope. Discovery history is not a logical proof dependency.

reading.title: From local clues to whole-fiber statements
reading.text: Minimality did not restore uniqueness; local isolation did not imply global uniqueness; the first-order opening threshold was not sharp. These failures made exact global support exhaustion indispensable. The later audit separated stable generator recovery from unstable entropy.

views.title: Keep the rejected statements visible
views.description: Eight exact failures prevent common overgeneralizations. Red “FALSIFIED” nodes are the old claims; red-role “PROVED” nodes are their verified counterexamples.

reading.title: Failed search is a different category
reading.text: A negative optimizer run remains inconclusive. An exact admissible witness can falsify a quantified claim. The graph preserves both, using tests for attempted searches and falsifies for actual counterexamples.

views.title: The novelty claim is deliberately narrow
views.description: Closest known mechanisms surround the physical theorem candidates. Each paper node records its observation model, quantity, assumptions, exact difference and access status.

reading.title: What is potentially new
reading.text: Credit zero forcing, normalized-similarity equivalence, hidden thermodynamic ambiguity and entropy singularity. The proposed advance is the precise coverage classification, finite bounded-measurement inverse and all-source complete-network entropy divergence. The bounded comparison does not certify priority.

views.title: Changing the model class changes the answer
views.description: Choose a theorem to inspect physical, observation, structural and technical assumptions, plus tested weakenings and counterexamples.

reading.title: Two assumptions that became clearer
reading.text: A supplied common rate cap is unnecessary for joint-kernel three-state continuity, but remains in the saved stationary-window argument. Fixed trace supplies a sufficient finite rate cap for the general construction; an arbitrary additional tight cap can instead freeze the entire model class.

views.title: Same data, different entropy geometry
views.description: Explore the exact balanced-theta regimes, then inspect a reproducible plot of the smallest fixed-trace divergence family. Schematic geometry and quantitative calculations are labeled separately.

reading.title: A bounded set need not be an interval
reading.text: At the quartic endpoint, there are exactly two physical generators modulo hidden labels and two distinct entropy values. The subcritical regime is unbounded; no finite numerical maximum is shown as its boundary. The three-state plot illustrates an analytic limit, not evidence for a new theorem.

views.title: What is settled—and what is still open
